Episode 228. Battle of Grosh and the Castle (8)
Her tone was closer to a command than a warning.
Kun looked at Luna with undisguised displeasure. Except for Beradin and Elona in Ziep, no one had the audacity to speak to him so rudely.
'What's with the commands? So what if she is a White Whale, what am I supposed to do?'
Luna maintained an impassive face against Kun's disgruntled gaze.
'...No, based on what she just said, they also want to avoid combat with us as much as possible, right? Then why is she picking a fight?'
With each passing second, a myriad of thoughts floated in Kun's mind.

'What's going on? If I don't back down, is she really planning to fight? Damn it, that's a bit overwhelming. It means defying the Supreme's command… Above all, can I win if I fight? It seemed doable when I heard about her from rumors, but meeting her in person... she seems pretty tough. Are there such monsters out there? Is she really not from Changsung?'
Overwhelming.
Kun was slowly regretting starting a staring contest with Luna. He should have just brushed off her provocation and casually told his troops to retreat. Retreating now would be a loss of face.
"Hey, Kun. Didn't you hear what the first generation said? Should I remind you again?"
As soon as Runtia added her comment, Kun almost flinched.
Unlike Luna, Runtia was brimming with a cold murderous aura, ready to tear Kun apart at any moment. The protective shield of the Ziep fleet vibrated under her aura.
Kun calmed his startled heart and lowered his head.
"Humph! Geez. You're so scary, and you're not even a thug. There's no point in fighting each other before catching the public enemy, yet you're so rude."
"It's not like Runcandel and Ziep have the right to speak of manners. We are thugs to each other, aren't we, Sogungju?"
"…You're right, third generation. The first generation just gave Ziep an opportunity to preserve its fleet, but this guy is overreacting."
"Ah! Fine, you're so great. I guess the more rational one has to yield. All fleet, retreat. We will re-enter after the front is organized."
In the end, Kun gave the order. Cold sweat ran down his back. As soon as the fleet retreated, Luna smiled at him.
"A wise choice. I'll remember today's incident, Koon."
Koon didn't answer and returned to the bridge of the flagship Fistrow.
"Well done, Captain Koon."
Suryong Ti-Ell stood beside Koon and spoke.

"Hoo, at least most of our forces are bio-golems, so our dignity seems to be less damaged. Please control the rest of the dragons and humans, Ti-Ell. I mean, I brushed it off, but anyone can see that I was flustered."
"After the Warlord surpassed fifteen, a saying arose among us in Zipfel. Never simply fight Luna Luncandel. Only fight her when she has made a fatal mistake herself."
The moment Ti-Ell finished speaking.

Beyond the bridge, hundreds of meteor showers were falling. The violet protective shield surrounding the entire right defense line shattered like glass, and most of the demons who came out to counterattack were swept away by the meteor shower and shockwaves, disappearing without a trace.
"Oh, shit... What's that, thought it was Ellona. This is crazy, this is insane."
"So, don't take it as a disgrace. It's actually commendable to have appropriately withdrawn against a Warlord."
Luna, moreover, unfolded a deluge along with a meteor shower and in a blink of an eye completely shattered the demons' protective shield with her tremendous power.

In just over ten seconds, she completely broke the front line in front of the right defense line. Of course, that huge shock wave was hitting the protective shield of Zipfel, which had retreated quite a distance.
If Koon hadn't withdrawn the fleet in order to preserve his pride, what would have happened is clear.
"Your words give me some comfort, Ti-Ell. Well, they said they would handle the annoying part first, so there was no reason to refuse."

"That's right, Captain. The bear shows off the skills, and we take the money... no, the opposite. The bear shows off the skills, and we take the money. We just need to take the biggest credit by shining at the right time."
Koon and Ti-Ell chuckled like fools and clapped their hands. Every once in a while, when a big shock was felt from Luna's side, their laughter would stop abruptly and they would be startled.
"Open the way. The minions can't stop us anyway."

Luntia shouted, firing her sword's energy. Three ships of the Demon World's fleet were split in half by that energy, and the resulting explosion of the power source engulfed the nearby demons in flames.
The battle was unfolding in a structure where Luna and Luntia were each breaking through one side and committing one-sided slaughter.

Cyrus, together with Mote, stationed himself behind Luna and Luntia, constantly creating ice platforms for them to step on. Occasionally, he caused snowstorms, gathering the enemies together for the knights to kill more effectively.

It might seem like a minor role at first glance, but it's not. Predicting the speed and path of the Luncandel knights and creating appropriate platforms every moment required an exceptional ability to read the battle.
"Block them! Block with your bodies, delay those humans from advancing even a second more!"

The general who issued the order met death more quickly due to his location being exposed by his voice. The riders were not slaughtering enemies randomly, but always first destroyed the ones in command.
They ensured that the enemies could neither give nor receive tactical commands. And no matter how large a number an army is, without proper command it becomes merely a rabble.
Realizing this fact, the demon commanders couldn't help but hesitate to issue orders. As soon as they made a peep, their heads would fall off or their bodies would be ripped into pieces.
Boom, Bang…!
Therefore, the demons started using signal flares, but even that was ineffective.
Before the signal flares could shoot high into the sky to deliver their message, the riders’ swords cut them down.
Despite the frantic battle, where hundreds of demons were slaughtered every second and new soldiers took their places, Luna and Runetia never missed a signal flare's location.
In other words, the many demons gathered at the right frontline were unable to communicate with each other at all. It felt like they were trapped in the dark rather than being on a battlefield.
Moreover, the right front line was relatively weak, as it was staffed by weaker demons compared to other front lines.
This was because priority was given to other fronts that were being directly attacked by the Bamuel Alliance, the Lutero Magic Federation, and the main force of Kinsel.
It is true that the number of demon soldiers reaches billions, but most of them have not yet escaped from hell.
In other words, with only the forces that have surfaced, it is inevitable that there would be gaps in the Grosh Fortress.

"You've been bothering us with headcounts and dimensional rifts, but it seems like your underbelly is beginning to show. The Human Race has begun to strike Grosh Fortress directly, but the number of rifts in our territory hasn't increased."
Luna spoke as she struck the back of a general trying to flee alone. Her crimson sword aura was tormenting him, infesting his wounds like a plague.
"Argh……!"
"Judging by the feel of the cut, you seem to be a general of sorts. But where were you trying to run away, leaving all these subordinates behind?"
The general was unable to answer due to the pain of the red sword aura invading his body and mind. Luna didn't care anyway. She didn't ask the question expecting an answer.

"Grosh Fortress? Even if you manage to teleport inside the fortress with your fancy magic, you'll end up meeting me again. Or your real headquarters underground? Even if you flee there, you'll eventually meet me again."
"Ugh."

"Nowhere on the surface or underground, nowhere in this world, exists a land where you can flee and survive. Therefore, you should, if possible, stand against me honorably and die in battle. Wouldn't it be regrettable if your last memory before death was merely of running away?"
Her faint voice amplified in an instant, reverberating throughout the entire battlefield. Not only the demons, but also the fleet of Zifl, cautiously advancing from the rear, heard her clearly.

"I am aware that none of you will plead for mercy or surrender. You've already missed the opportunity given by our High God. So, raise your swords against me with proud eyes, prove to me that there is at least one amongst you worthy of being cut down by this Khrantel."
Before the corpse of the recently slain general had completely disintegrated under her red power, two more generals were meeting their demise under the strikes of Luna and Runtia.
Swoosh...

Countless unnamed soldiers lost their lives to the wave of sword energy spreading like a tsunami. Most of the demons were unaware of the riders' swords killing them, they only heard Luna's voice clearly.
Despite having slain so many enemies, neither of the two showed signs of fatigue. Their hair remained dry, and their breaths were steady.
Soon, within a radius of a thousand steps around them, not a single demon remained alive. Corpses burning or disintegrating into particles were the only things indifferently rolling like sea foam.
But even the demons a thousand steps away were within the range of their attack, they were no different from being already dead.
The riders trod on the ice path created by Sirius, slowly moving forward. As they approached, the demons on the defensive line backed away like frightened beasts.
Even before the riders swung their swords, the line crumbled, and the commanders were still unable to issue commands aloud.
"Runtia."
"Yes, sister."
"Let's speed up a bit now. It looks like our youngest is about to break through to the third defensive line soon, so we should match the pace. Besides, this area is mainly composed of weaker ones."
"You mean, don't give Zifl a chance to take the glory. Fine, the protagonists who subjugated the demonic realm in history should be us."
Luna and Runtia readjusted their postures with impassive faces. As they began to ramp up their energy in earnest, the sea vibrated, and large whirlpools formed here and there.
